points.description: States that a tree is a collection of nodes (a non-empty set of nodes), using the term 'nodes'.
States that the collection has one special node called the root.

States that the remaining nodes (other than the root) are partitioned into one or more disjoint sets, with the term 'disjoint' (non-overlapping) used, and each such set is itself a tree (recursive definition, i.e. subtrees).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if clearly states the rest of the nodes are split into disjoint sets/subtrees but omits that each set is itself a tree (or the reverse)

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise recursive definition: a collection of nodes, one special node called the root, and the remaining nodes partitioned into one or more disjoint sets each of which is a tree. Generic statements (e.g. 'hierarchical structure', 'nodes connected by edges', 'parent and children') without these elements earn nothing for the matching point. Part marks only on P3 as stated; a wrong statement about a point (e.g. allowing cycles or multiple roots) loses that point.
